neighbours.label: reading off what a high or low number on a graded scale means (a higher gauge number means a thinner wire), as opposed to the same 'higher X means Y' frame with a quantity that is not a grade, including a number of things
fire: A higher grit number means finer sandpaper.
On the Beaufort scale, a higher number means a stronger wind.
A lower handicap indicates a stronger golfer.
A higher octane rating means the fuel resists knocking.
A lower f-stop means a wider opening in the lens.
The higher the Scoville rating, the hotter the pepper.
Lower values on the Kelvin scale mean warmer light from the bulb.
A higher UV index means a greater risk of sunburn.
quiet: A higher salary means finer furniture.
On the coast road, a higher speed means a worse crash.
A lower fence invites a stronger thief.
A higher number of hills means the road needs more bends.
A lower ceiling means a smaller room in the house.
The higher the mountain, the colder the air.
Lower prices on the market mean cheaper bread for the town.
A larger number of guests means a longer table.

short: what a number on a scale means
notes: Card: ' magnitude' x2, ' greater', ' True', ' lowest', ' lower', on scales where direction needs explaining (star magnitude, f-numbers, film speed). Probes: 0.22-0.63 on gauge, Mohs, Richter, SPF, pH, f-numbers and golf, often peaking on ' means'; 'higher wage means' 0.06, 'larger house means' 0.02, 'lower taxes mean' 0.04, 'the lower the sun' 0.13, a dial listed without a reading 0.01. A reversed scale is not required (Richter 0.41), so that part of my first idea was dropped. 'Sirius has a magnitude' 0.18.
